$comment: MIG-02 (D-15/D-16/D-17): the single machine-readable source of truth for the Sourcerer -> Power Browser rename. It has exactly two consumers, and they read this same file so that what is scanned and what is renamed cannot drift apart: scripts/rename-brand.mjs (the rerunnable rename executor) and scripts/scan-brand-residue.mjs (the residual-brand scan and its reconciled red-scan evidence). FAIL-CLOSED RULE: an occurrence found in the migrating scope that no row here accounts for is a FAILURE, never silently ignored -- that is reconciliation condition 4, and it is the one condition that catches an under-scanning scanner rather than a stale inventory. rename-brand.mjs refuses to run at all while any row lacks a `class` from the five-value set, so this file is the gate, not documentation. Per-row keys: `token`; `case_form` (lower | title | upper | literal -- the three case forms are three DIFFERENT tokens matched case-sensitively, per Pitfall 1; `literal` is a structural or site anchor matched as a raw substring with no boundary rule); `class` (brand-identifier | brand-display | identity | frozen | coincidental); `target`; `expected_count` and `expected_files[]` (measured against this tree, and reconciled against research's independent ground truth in 01-SCAN-RED-REPORT.md); `couples_with[]` (paths whose sites must move in the SAME pass, per Pitfall 2); `stage` (the cross-tier contract group a row belongs to, so plan 01-02 can stage commits by CONTRACT rather than by tier -- Pitfall 3); `reason` (mandatory on every frozen and coincidental row, citing file:line evidence); `only_in[]` (restricts a row to named files, and OUTRANKS the broad row for the same literal -- this is how the ambiguous TitleCase form is classified per site rather than per token); and `site_overrides[]` of {file, line, class, target, reason} for the same purpose keyed by line. Prefer `only_in` with a longer context-anchored token over `site_overrides`: a pinned line number silently stops meaning anything the moment an edit above it shifts the file.

scope.include: Every path `git ls-files` reports from the repo root, minus the `exclude` prefixes below, minus any path ending in one of `binary_extensions`. Derived from git rather than from a hand-kept list because git already excludes every ignored path -- upstream/, objdir/, objdir-release/, .mozbuild/, node_modules/, theia/**/lib/ -- which is the half of Pitfall 7 that drowns the scan in Gecko's own thousands of firefox-named files.
scope.exclude_reason: .planning/ is this repo's own planning record, not migrating source; it quotes the Sourcerer tokens as historical evidence and renaming it would destroy the provenance D-08 protects. inventory/ and the two rename scripts are the rename's own machinery: they necessarily spell out every token, so scanning them would be scanning the scan's own input -- vacuous, and it would make the tree permanently red. Every other tracked path is in scope, including docs/, README.md, LICENSE, .mozconfig, patches/, theia/ and the rest of scripts/.
scope.residue_probes_reason: Used ONLY by reconciliation condition 4, and deliberately NOT by the boundary matcher: a raw case-insensitive substring search with no boundary rule at all. Every probe hit must land inside a span some row below claimed. A bug in the boundary matcher (missing `sourcererPrivilegedJs`, say) therefore leaves an unclaimed probe hit and fails condition 4, even though conditions 1-3 would all agree with themselves. This is the independent source T-01-04 requires -- the rename script never writes it.

ground_truth.$comment: D-17 says a non-zero exit is not evidence, because an under-scanning scanner also exits non-zero. This block is the outside number the scan is checked against: 01-RESEARCH.md counted the sourcerer tree independently, with grep, before any of this tooling existed. scan-brand-residue.mjs recounts `raw_forms` the same dumb way -- plain case-sensitive substring over the scanned scope, no rows and no boundary rule -- and asserts that observed + already_renamed + not_imported equals migrating_occurrences + phase_verifier_occurrences EXACTLY. Every line below is a named deviation rather than a fudge factor, which is the difference between reconciling a count and absorbing one.
ground_truth.source: 01-RESEARCH.md, "Token Inventory Ground Truth -> Occurrence counts by migration disposition", measured over `git ls-files` at sourcerer@bce68bb468e4dc160da8c9e238e030a400b806f8 with a clean working tree
ground_truth.phase_verifier_note: scripts/verify-phase-0{2,3,4,5}.sh. Research counted them separately because their disposition was undecided; D-21 decided it -- the checks were migrated and then consolidated into scripts/verify-platform.sh in plan 01-03, which DELETED all four driver files. Their occurrences were inside this scan's scope when this census was taken and are accounted for here; the four paths no longer exist on disk.
ground_truth.census_status: HISTORICAL -- PRE-RENAME, AND DELIBERATELY NOT REWRITTEN (plan 01-03's call, deferred to it by 01-02). Everything in this `ground_truth` block and every `expected_count` / `expected_files` on a row below describes the tree AT THE IMPORT COMMIT, before scripts/rename-brand.mjs ran. That is what made 01-SCAN-RED-REPORT.md a checkable artifact: a red scan reconciled against an independently-grepped outside number is evidence, whereas a non-zero exit alone is not, because an UNDER-scanning scanner also exits non-zero (D-17). Post-rename, `--reconcile` reports condition failures and a large negative ground-truth deviation. That is the census correctly describing a tree that no longer exists -- it is not a live defect and it is not the gate. THE GATE IS THE PLAIN RUN: `node scripts/scan-brand-residue.mjs`, no flags, which is what scripts/rebase-upstream.sh, the CI rebase workflow, and verify-platform.sh's `scan-brand-residue` check all invoke, and which exits 0 over the current tree. Rewriting these numbers to the post-rename tree was considered and REJECTED: post-rename every count is zero by construction, so the rewritten census would assert nothing the plain gate does not already assert, while destroying the only record of what the pre-rename tree actually contained. An all-zeros census is a vacuous duplicate of a gate that already works. The `expected_files` arrays are likewise left pointing at pre-rename paths where a file has since moved or been deleted -- they are provenance, the same reason D-08 freezes the historical plan-file citations rather than renumbering them.

already_renamed.what: the `chrome-package` coupled chain, renamed by the tracer in plan 01-01 before this report was produced

not_imported.reason: Sourcerer's own agent instructions. Left downstream by the plan 01-01 import alongside the D-03 exclusions; research's census predates that decision and still counts it.
Same: Sourcerer's agent configuration, not platform source.

chrome-package.reason: The chrome://sourcerer/ coupled chain, renamed end-to-end by the tracer in plan 01-01 before the machinery was pointed at the rest of the tree: the chrome package name and its six jar.mn registration lines, the components.conf esModule and constructor keys, the moz.build JAR_MANIFESTS / DEFINES / JS_PREFERENCE_PP_FILES / XPCOM_MANIFESTS wiring, the reference inside patches/020, and the two chrome-package allowlist globs in check-internals-boundary.sh -- six coupled reference formats that must move together or the build packages a chrome package nothing can reach. `--scope-chain` narrows the FILE SET only; every row stays active, so a chain run is the full ruleset restricted to these files.

brand_display_expectations.$comment: THE EXPECTED-VALUE SOURCE for scripts/verify-branding-preflight.mjs, and the reason that script is not a tautology. Authored by hand in plan 01-03 from the RECORDED IDENTITY DECISIONS (01-CONTEXT.md D-09 as amended, D-10, D-12, D-13) -- not read back out of the branding files, not produced by scripts/rename-brand.mjs, and not derived from scripts/verify-branding-identity.mjs's VARIANTS descriptor. That independence is the whole point: Pitfall 1's failure mode is a mechanical pass that rewrites BOTH a display literal and the expectation that checks it, so the build succeeds, the window title is wrong, and the verifier agrees. It actually happened -- the rename left verify-branding-identity.mjs expecting `PowerBrowser Dev`, the space-less identifier form, and nothing in the tree disagreed with it. A third source that no pass writes is the only thing that catches that. The `tokens` rows below carry the same targets as COUNTS (how many occurrences per file); this block carries them as VALUES (which literal at which named key), and the preflight asserts both.
brand_display_expectations.vendor_split_reason: D-09 as amended 2026-08-30. MOZ_APP_VENDOR is lowercased and concatenated into the Firefox profile path with no space stripping (upstream/toolkit/xre/nsXREDirProvider.cpp:1621-1637), so the display-side `DeBIOS Foundation` would yield `~/.config/debios foundation/powerbrowser/` -- a space in a path, against this repo's hard no-spaces rule. The two values MUST be distinct and the preflight asserts that they are: collapsing them either puts a space in the profile path or ships a vendor string that is not the foundation's name.
brand_display_expectations.identifier_form_reason: D-10's TitleCase identifier prefix. It is listed here as the value that must NEVER appear in a display string -- the preflight asserts its absence from every display surface, because `PowerBrowser Dev` is exactly what a token-boundary rename produces and exactly what nothing else in the tree would object to.

hand_write.$comment: Surfaces rename-brand.mjs is forbidden to touch, in addition to every `brand-display` and `frozen` row, which it skips by class. These are hand-written in plan 01-03. The display literals are Pitfall 1: `Sourcerer` here means `Power Browser` (two words, with the space), and a mechanical pass gets them wrong while the verifier that checks them AGREES, because the same pass rewrote both sides. The `.desktop` files are excluded for a second, independent reason (Pitfall 4): three tokens on one `Icon=`/`Exec=` line with three different correct targets, which no token-boundary rule can get right.

line_contains.reason: theia/applications/browser/package.json:13 -- `"applicationName": "Sourcerer"` is a display literal whose target is `Power Browser`, but the rest of this file carries ordinary identifier occurrences the script must rename. Excluding the whole file would leave those behind, so the exclusion is line-scoped.
LICENSE:133 -- the MPL Exhibit B notice names a legal entity, not an identifier. Rewritten whole by hand in plan 01-03.

tokens.reason: scripts/verify-branding-identity.mjs:31 -- a comment recording the live application.ini values this verifier asserts. It must move with the expectation on the same file's checkApplicationIni, or the comment documents a value the code no longer expects. Anchored on the surrounding literal rather than on a line number so an edit above it cannot silently retarget the rule.

scripts/verify-branding-identity.mjs:337 -- application.ini's Name comes from MOZ_APP_BASENAME, which .mozconfig's --with-app-basename sets. D-10 fixes that identifier at the one-word lowercase form `powerbrowser`, NOT the TitleCase display name, so this expectation is `powerbrowser` and is class identity rather than a mechanical case swap. Coupled to .mozconfig: if only one side moves the surface fails with a value mismatch that names neither cause.

.mozconfig:6 -- MOZ_APP_BASENAME is lowercased into the profile path (upstream/toolkit/xre/nsXREDirProvider.cpp:1621-1637) and surfaces as application.ini Name. D-10 fixes it at `powerbrowser`, one word, matching MOZ_APP_REMOTINGNAME and StartupWMClass. Anchored on the option text so the TitleCase-to-lowercase target cannot leak into the 300-odd other TitleCase sites.
Cross-tier: the cookie name the chrome side sets and the Node token gate reads. Longer than SOURCERER_TOKEN, so the longest-token-first claim order takes it first and the shorter row never splits it.
Cross-tier test bypass. smoke-theia.sh sets it, so a half-renamed tree still passes the smoke test while the real gate is broken -- the exact blind spot Pitfall 3 names.
Cross-tier stdout sentinel: the Node backend prints it, the chrome side waits for it. Renamed on one side only, the chrome side waits forever and reports a timeout that names nothing.

Cross-tier stdout sentinel AND half of the verifier regex at scripts/verify-branding-identity.mjs:347, which embeds two brand tokens (this one and the [SourcererAPI] console-mirror prefix). Pitfall 2: rename the emitter without the regex and the surface fails with "did not appear within Nms", a timeout that names no cause.
Cross-tier env var: the chrome side sets it when spawning the backend, the parent watchdog reads it. Split across commits, the watchdog silently stops supervising.

Cross-tier auth-token env var, minted at runtime by TheiaService.sys.mjs and read by the Node token gate. Split across commits, the backend boots and rejects every request with a 403 that names no cause -- and smoke-theia.sh still passes, because it sets the disable bypass.

Coupled format 3: a mozbuild DEFINES[] name consumed as the `@SOURCERER_DEV_TREE@` substitution token in the preprocessed sidecar pref file. The define and the substitution token must rename together or the pref carries a literal unsubstituted path and the backend never starts. The moz.build half already moved with the chrome-package chain; the sidecar half is what remains.

Coupled format 5: scripts/verify-dev-flag-off.mjs:68 carries the symbol key inside a STRING evaluated in the page (`Symbol.for('SourcererPrivilegedJs')`), so TypeScript cannot catch a drift between it and the module that registers the symbol. Both sides are listed in couples_with.

Coupled format 4/6: scripts/apply-patches.sh's run_self_test() hardcodes this patch filename, so the file rename and the self-test's literal must move together or the self-test silently stops testing anything. Its sibling 020-sourcerer-shell.patch gets no row of its own because no file NAMES it -- only 010 is referenced by a literal -- so its rename is entirely a git mv, which plan 01-02 owns. Both patch files' CONTENT is regenerated from a patched tree in plan 01-04, never text-edited: editing a .patch invalidates the index blob hashes that make `git apply --3way` a real 3-way merge, and 010's post-image hash is literally 020's pre-image hash.

Coupled formats 1/2/5/6 at once: the parenthesised source filename in jar.mn, the esModule chrome:// URL in components.conf, the exempt-file basename and catalogue target in check-internals-boundary.sh, every catalogue row in INTERNAL-APIS.md, and the console-mirror prefix inside scripts/verify-branding-identity.mjs:347's regex. Given its own row so that coupling is declared rather than left to the broad TitleCase pass.

COUNT MOVED 4 -> 0 (plan 01-08, reconciling against the tree as it stands). The tree change that moved it: plan 01-03 hand-wrote both .desktop entries, rewriting all four sites -- Exec= and Icon= in each file -- to this repo's own root /home/chris/coding/Power-Browser. The four occurrences are gone because the hand-write this row exists to protect actually happened, not because the row stopped being enforced. ZERO IS LOAD-BEARING HERE, exactly as it is on the #130829 row below: the row stays coincidental with a zero count so a rebase or a copied desktop entry that reintroduces the old absolute path fails by name, and so scripts/verify-branding-preflight.mjs's coincidental-zero assertion -- which only asserts against rows that are BOTH coincidental AND zero -- becomes active on it. Original rationale, still the reason this is a row at all: sourcerer/sourcerer.desktop:3-4 and sourcerer-release.desktop:3-4 -- the ABSOLUTE REPO ROOT, which is not the product identifier and does not take the `powerbrowser` target. `Exec=/home/chris/coding/sourcerer/objdir/dist/bin/sourcerer` carries three tokens with three different correct targets on one line; a token-boundary rename produces a path that does not exist, the script reports success, and the desktop entry silently does nothing when clicked (Pitfall 4). Classified coincidental so the scan REPORTS it and the rename script leaves it alone; both .desktop files are hand-written in plan 01-03. Longer than the bare `sourcerer` token, so the claim order takes the repo root first and the tree directory after it.

MOZILLA'S BRAND PURPLE, not a neutral, and it was sitting inside Power Browser's branding directory at branding/{dev,release}/content/aboutDialog.css:7 -- invisible to this scan for its whole life, because the boundary matcher matches brand TOKENS (`sourcerer`, `deocracy`) and never a hex. 01-UI-SPEC.md "Color -> Residual Mozilla brand value" requires it replaced with the shell's dominant neutral #1a1a1a, which plan 01-03 did. EXPECTED_COUNT IS 0 ON PURPOSE: the row exists so a rebase that reintroduces the value is caught by name rather than rediscovered, and so Phase 6's static scan inherits the knowledge instead of re-deriving it. Class coincidental rather than brand-display because the string is a colour value, not a name -- it takes a target but is not a presentation of the product.

The translucent form of the SAME Mozilla brand hue as the row above, at branding/{dev,release}/content/aboutDialog.css:13. Given its own row rather than folded into the hex row because it is a different notation of the same value and a scan for one would not find the other -- the same token-SET reasoning Pitfall 8 applies to the vendor. Replaced with rgba(17, 17, 17, 0.5), the shell's diagnostics-well neutral #111 at fifty percent, per 01-UI-SPEC.md "Color". expected_count 0 for the same reason as the row above.

sourcerer/branding/dev/locales/en-US/brand.ftl:5-8,11 -- -brand-shorter-name, -brand-short-name, -brand-shortcut-name, -brand-full-name, and the D-78 rationale comment naming the product. Display literal: the target is `Power Browser`, TWO WORDS WITH A SPACE, not the identifier `PowerBrowser`. Hand-written in plan 01-03. This is Pitfall 1's exact trap: a mechanical pass writes `PowerBrowser Dev`, the build succeeds, and verify-branding-identity.mjs surface 4 AGREES because the same pass rewrote the descriptor it compares against.

sourcerer/branding/release/locales/en-US/brand.ftl:5-8,11 -- the release variant of the same four terms plus the D-78 comment. -brand-full-name here is bare `Sourcerer` (no " Dev"), so the release display name is `Power Browser` and the dev one is `Power Browser Dev`; D-13 keeps both presentations.

sourcerer/branding/dev/locales/en-US/brand.properties:5-7 -- brandShorterName, brandShortName, brandFullName. The .properties file is the second half of the same display surface as brand.ftl and verify-branding-identity.mjs asserts BOTH against the variant's expected value, so they must be hand-written to the same literal.
sourcerer/branding/release/locales/en-US/brand.properties:5-7 -- the release variant of the same three keys.

sourcerer/branding/dev/configure.sh:5 -- MOZ_APP_DISPLAYNAME="Sourcerer Dev". A COMPILED define: Pitfall 6 measures a full tier-3 rebuild at ~39 minutes, so a typo here costs 40 minutes, which is why every display literal is hand-written and cross-checked before the first build rather than iterated on.
sourcerer/branding/release/configure.sh:5 -- MOZ_APP_DISPLAYNAME="Sourcerer", the release variant.

sourcerer/sourcerer.desktop:2 -- `Name=Sourcerer Dev` takes the DISPLAY form while `StartupWMClass=sourcerer` on line 8 takes the identifier form, in the same nine-line file. The whole file is hand-written in plan 01-03 (see hand_write.files) for the separate Pitfall 4 reason.
sourcerer/sourcerer-release.desktop:2 -- the release desktop entry's Name=. Same split as the dev entry.

theia/applications/browser/package.json:13 -- `"applicationName": "Sourcerer"` is the Theia frontend's window/title display name. The rest of this file carries ordinary lowercase identifier occurrences the rename script DOES handle, so the exclusion is line-scoped in hand_write.line_contains rather than whole-file.

LICENSE:133 -- the MPL Exhibit B "Required Notice" line, `Copyright Deocracy Institute Corporation (Sourcerer)`. A legal notice, not an identifier: the whole line is rewritten by hand in plan 01-03 to the DeBIOS Foundation's own notice. Held out of the script because a token-wise pass would produce "DeBIOS Foundation Institute Corporation", which is not a legal entity.

sourcerer/branding/dev/locales/en-US/brand.ftl:15 -- `-vendor-short-name` is the DISPLAY-side vendor string, so its target is `DeBIOS Foundation` (D-09 as amended 2026-08-30), NOT the path-forming `DeBIOS` that MOZ_APP_VENDOR takes. The residual scan and verify-branding-identity.mjs must treat these as two distinct expected values -- that is the whole point of the amendment, since "DeBIOS Foundation" lowercased into a profile path would put a space in a path.
sourcerer/branding/release/locales/en-US/brand.ftl:15 -- the release variant's display-side vendor string. Same split as the dev variant.
LICENSE:133 -- the vendor half of the same MPL Required Notice line. Hand-written with the rest of the line in plan 01-03.

The XPCOM contract-id DNS namespace, `@sourcerer.dev/single-instance-clh;1`. Class identity, not brand-identifier, because the target is a decision rather than a case swap: the DeBIOS Foundation does not own a .dev domain, and D-12 establishes powerbrowser.org (T-01-05). EXPECTED_COUNT IS 0 ON PURPOSE -- its one site, sourcerer/shell/components.conf:17, already moved with the chrome-package chain in plan 01-01. expected_files still names that file because it is where the row is anchored; the row is kept as the standing record of the decision and as the classification any reappearance of the token would land in.

The UPPER_SNAKE form: env vars, dump()/stdout sentinels, TS exports and build defines. Matched with an UPPER_SNAKE join allowed on either side, so `SOURCERER_SHELL_READY` matches while `SOURCERERX` would not. The six cross-tier contracts above carry their own longer rows and a `stage`, so this row is everything that is NOT a cross-tier contract.

TitleCase AS AN IDENTIFIER PREFIX -- class and symbol names, target `PowerBrowser` with no space. Every display site is carved out above by a file-scoped brand-display row that outranks this one, which is how the same nine characters resolve to two different targets per site (Pitfall 1). This row is the identifier remainder.

The fixed-identifier form (D-10, one word so camelCase collapses into it rather than needing a sixth case variant). Matched with a camelCase join allowed on the right and no token character on the left, so `sourcererPrivilegedJs` matches while `resourcerer` does not -- both proved by the rename script's --self-test.

The PATH-FORMING vendor value: MOZ_APP_VENDOR in patches/010 and the expectation that reads it back in verify-branding-identity.mjs. D-09 as amended splits the vendor in two -- `DeBIOS` compiled (it is lowercased into ~/.config/<vendor>/<basename>, and a space there breaks the no-spaces repo rule this project builds under) and `DeBIOS Foundation` on display. The rename pass carried the endpoint-allowlist.json and welcome-widget URLs to github.com/DeBIOS/PowerBrowser, an org the foundation has never established; plan 01-03 retargeted both at https://powerbrowser.org/, the one host D-12 actually fixes, so no shipped link points at a namespace a third party could claim.

The lowercase vendor form: `--with-distribution-id=org.deocracy` becomes `org.debios`, and the `~/.config/deocracy/sourcerer` profile-path comment in verify-endpoints.sh becomes `~/.config/debios/powerbrowser`. Seeded explicitly because Pitfall 8 is that the vendor token is invisible to a scan for three case forms of "sourcerer" -- it is a token SET, not a search for one string.

sourcerer/shell/components.conf:16 -- the XPCOM class id. Nothing keys off its value, so regenerating it is pure churn in a bisect. Held back by class and asserted still present by count after the rename.

sourcerer/shell/components.conf:20 -- the `a-` category-entry PREFIX is frozen while the brand suffix after it is not. The file's own comment states the mechanism: the name sorts ahead of the stock handler's "m-browser" and far ahead of "x-default" under ascending strcmp (upstream/xpcom/components/nsCategoryManager.cpp:210-213), and that ordering IS the single-instance mechanism. Claiming this literal first leaves the following token with a `-` on its left, a legal boundary, so the site becomes `a-powerbrowser` -- still ahead of both.

sourcerer/branding/{dev,release}/content/jar.mn:12 -- `branding` here is Gecko's OWN chrome slot name, not this product's brand. Renaming it detaches the branding package from every stock consumer of chrome://branding/content/.
sourcerer/branding/{dev,release}/locales/jar.mn:10 -- the locale half of the same stock Gecko slot. Upstream's name, never ours.

sourcerer/branding/dev/locales/en-US/brand.ftl:14 and sourcerer/branding/release/locales/en-US/brand.ftl:14 -- deliberately NOT the product name (D-78). A small set of "requires Firefox" compatibility strings interpolate this term, and byte-identical UA/product naming is the same rationale D-78 already applied to the User-Agent. Its rationale comment sits directly above it and migrates verbatim under D-08.

COUNT MOVED 2 -> 1 (plan 01-08). The tree change that moved it: the second site was never a define of its own -- it was a CONTEXT LINE that patch 020 happened to carry, and patch 020 was regenerated during plan 01-05's browser-window work (it no longer overrides BROWSER_CHROME_URL), which changed its hunk context and dropped the line. The define itself is untouched and still pinned at its one real site, patches/010-powerbrowser-identity.patch, which is what expected_files now names: the row exists to prove the define stayed pinned, so it must keep naming a site that carries it rather than a stale second file. Original rationale: pinned to "Firefox" on purpose so the User-Agent stays byte-identical to Firefox's. Neither the option name nor its value is a brand token here.

COUNT MOVED 2 -> 1 (plan 01-08). Same tree change as the MOZ_APP_UA_NAME row above and for the same reason: the second occurrence was a context line in patch 020, and patch 020 was regenerated during plan 01-05's browser-window work, which changed its hunk context and dropped the line. The define is untouched at its one real site, which expected_files now names. Original rationale: deliberately Firefox's own app id {ec8030f7-c20a-464f-9b0e-13a3a9e97384}, so installed extensions keep resolving. Changing it silently breaks extension compatibility with no build failure.

COUNT MOVED 21 -> 28 (plan 01-08), and NOT ONE HISTORICAL CITATION WAS RENUMBERED OR DELETED to get there -- the whole point of the row would be destroyed by that. The census of 21 was taken at the inventory's seeding commit and is reconciled here by name against two tree changes, both of which ADD: (a) +2 from the driver consolidation. Plan 01-03 deleted verify-phase-03.sh, -04.sh and -05.sh, which carried 1, 1 and 3 citations, and consolidated them into scripts/verify-platform.sh, which now carries 7: those same 5 ported verbatim, plus 2 new 01-04 citations that plan added. expected_files therefore drops the three deleted drivers and names the consolidated driver, which is where those citations now live. (b) +5 from powerbrowser/INTERNAL-APIS.md, which grew from 6 citations to 11 when plan 01-05 catalogued its GUI-01 touchpoints, each carrying its own 01-05 provenance citation. The six historical Sourcerer-era citations in that file (05-01 x1, 05-03 x3, 05-04 x2) are byte-identical to the census-era set. 21 + 2 + 5 = 28, closing by name with nothing absorbed. Original rationale: D-08: the historical Sourcerer plan-file citations carried in migrated comments (04-01-PLAN.md, 05-01-PLAN.md and the rest) are PROVENANCE, not brand. They name plans that live in the frozen sourcerer repo and renumbering or deleting them destroys the only trail back to why the code is shaped the way it is. Anchored on the filename suffix so the count assertion proves they all survived the rename; the decision-ID citations beside them (D-96/D-97, D-121, SIDE-04) carry no brand token and so cannot be touched by any row here at all.

Every Gecko pref key under branding/*/pref/firefox-branding.js is upstream's, not ours -- and none of them contains a brand token, so the only thing the rename touches in these two files is comment text naming the product or a repo path. This row's count is the assertion that the pref statements themselves came through untouched; verify-endpoints.sh layer 1 asserts each key's value against endpoint-allowlist.json on the installed, unpreprocessed copy.
